findings.reason: Verified that the url is put into `<a href='#{url}'>` without escaping inside a raw_html post that `Post#cook` returns unsanitised, and that an anonymous embed_url only has to pass a host check, so a quote in the query string can inject attributes and give stored XSS.

The throttle key and the unique embed index both use the exact URL, so adding new query strings gets past `retrieved_recently?` and creates a new topic each time; this is real abuse potential, although it needs a forged Referer.
`i.content.scrub` has no nil guard, and RSS 2.0 items that only have description (or only content:encoded) would crash the poll, and the inline call from TopicRetriever would crash with it.

`<%- end if %>` really is a stray modifier, but the next generated statement is a whitespace append that returns a truthy value, so the claimed consequences are hedged and probably never show up; mostly a typo.
It is correct that the spec depends on queue_jobs being false in tests, but this is a minor test-design concern.
The diff does remove the --category option and created_at from the Disqus import, and `import_remote` has no rescue, so this is a real behaviour regression in a dev tool.
The `indexOf` origin check really is a prefix/substring match, but a bypass only lets an attacker resize the iframe.
`force: true` was in fact added to an unrelated existing migration; it only matters in unusual database states.

Post includes Trashable, whose default_scope hides soft-deleted posts, so `embed.post` is nil even after an ordinary deletion, and if the feed content changes `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises and stops the poll.
